title: Microsoft Purview: legacy Teams retention policies will stop covering Copilot interactions
summary: The briefing's rollout dates, retention changes, billing prerequisites and portal paths are supported. Two minor corrections remain: disclose conflicting Microsoft guidance about the Copilot PowerShell syntax and its preview status, and reconcile the billing checklist with the controls table.

claims.claim: Some existing Teams-scoped retention policies currently also apply to Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions.
claims.quote: Some existing retention policies scoped to Microsoft Teams may currently also apply to Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to convert legacy Teams-and-Copilot retention policies to Teams-only policies that no longer implicitly govern Copilot.
claims.quote: As part of an upcoming change, these legacy Teams retention policies will be converted to—and treated as—Teams-only policies. They will no longer implicitly govern Copilot workloads.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Get output for legacy combined policies still shows MicrosoftTeams rather than TeamsChatUserInteractions after processing becomes Teams-only.
claims.quote: doing a Get command on 'Teams chats and Copilot interactions' policies from cmdlet will still show the policy covering teams+copilot i.e. MicrosoftTeams and NOT TeamsChatUserInteractions but while processing; they will ONLY cover Teams Interactions.

claims.claim: Microsoft describes no identity or permission change associated with this conversion.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview legacy Teams Copilot retention change identity permissions tenant notification conversion January 2027; "Teams chats and Copilot interactions" "identity" "permissions". Read MC1481313, create-retention-policies and get-started-with-data-lifecycle-management.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft does not explain conversion-specific release or deletion eligibility for interactions already held by a legacy policy.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams chats and Copilot interactions" "previously retained" released deletion; "Teams chats and Copilot interactions" "released". Read create-retention-policies, retention-policies-copilot and MC1481313; none explains the conversion-specific transition for already-held items.

claims.claim: A reliable conversion-specific identification method remains undocumented beyond the warning about misleading Get output.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams chats and Copilot interactions" identify legacy policy portal MicrosoftTeams. Read create-retention-policies, Get-RetentionCompliancePolicy and MC1481313; these describe review and the Get-output caveat, not a definitive conversion-identification procedure.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not specified a per-tenant notification when conversion completes.
claims.quote: Searched: "MC1481313" notification conversion applied tenant; "Teams chats and Copilot interactions" "notify". Read MC1481313 and create-retention-policies; neither specifies a per-tenant conversion-completion notification.

claims.where: licensing.notes; controls[1].note; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go billing must be set up to create policies including Microsoft Copilot experiences, Enterprise AI apps or Other AI apps.
claims.quote: You must set up pay-as-you-go billing to create retention policies that include the locations Microsoft Copilot experiences, Enterprise AI apps, and Other AI apps.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions are not charged for this retention capability.
claims.quote: There's no charge for Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions.

claims.claim: The Data Lifecycle Management meter counts non-Microsoft 365 Copilot or AI app prompts and responses under a retention policy.
claims.quote: Number of non-Microsoft 365 Copilot or AI App interactions (prompts and responses) under a retention policy

claims.claim: Learn directs readers to the Purview service description for feature-level licence requirements.
claims.quote: For the features listed on this page, see the Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management & Records Management section for feature-level licensing requirements.

claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed, combining licensing prerequisites with required pay-as-you-go setup while excluding Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions from charges.
claims.quote: The pay-as-you-go billing model builds on the per-user licensing model. The two are complementary, not mutually exclusive.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The known incremental cost of this change is administrator effort, rather than a charge for retaining Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions.
claims.quote: You must set up pay-as-you-go billing to create retention policies that include the locations Microsoft Copilot experiences, Enterprise AI apps, and Other AI apps. There's no charge for Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions.

claims.claim: Learn recommends the Compliance Administrator role group for people managing retention policies.
claims.quote: To grant permissions for this limited administration, we recommend that you add users to the Compliance Administrator admin role group.

claims.claim: A custom role group containing Retention Management is an alternative.
claims.quote: Alternatively to using this default role, you can create a new role group and add the Retention Management role to this group.

claims.claim: View-Only Retention Management provides read-only access.
claims.quote: For a read-only role, use View-Only Retention Management.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Creating and managing the replacement retention policy requires Purview portal retention permissions.
claims.quote: Members of your compliance team who will create and manage retention policies and retention labels need permissions to the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Tenant retention policies can be reviewed in Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies.

claims.claim: Get-RetentionCompliancePolicy -Identity "<policy name>" -DistributionDetail | Format-List retrieves detailed policy information including accurate distribution and location values.
claims.quote:
Get-RetentionCompliancePolicy -Identity "Regulation 123 Compliance" -DistributionDetail | Format-List
This example displays detailed information for the policy named "Regulation 123 Compliance", including accurate values for the DistributionStatus and *Location properties.

claims.claim: A Copilot retention policy starts at Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies > New retention policy, selecting Microsoft Copilot experiences.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies.
Select New retention policy to start the Create retention policy configuration, and name your new retention policy.

claims.claim: Set-AppRetentionCompliancePolicy -Identity "<policy name>" -Applications "User:M365Copilot" adds Copilot interactions to an existing policy for newer locations.
claims.quote:
To add Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions to an existing retention policy for newer locations, such as Teams private channel messages and Viva Engage:
Set-AppRetentionCompliancePolicy -Identity “<policy name>” -Applications "User:M365Copilot"
claims.fix: Append this qualification to the second control's note: 'Microsoft's configuration guide shows User:M365Copilot alone, but the cmdlet reference marks Microsoft Copilot experiences as preview and requires all application values together: User:M365Copilot,CopilotForSecurity,CopilotinFabricPowerBI,CopilotStudio,CopilotinBusinessApplicationplatformsSales,SQLCopilot. Confirm the supported syntax before running this example.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/set-appretentioncompliancepolicy#-applications. The cited configuration guide supports the printed command, so this is a disagreement between Microsoft pages, not an invented command.

claims.claim: Selecting Teams locations for a static retention policy excludes the other locations, requiring a separate Copilot policy.
claims.quote: If you select the Teams or Viva Engage locations when you create a retention policy, the other locations are automatically excluded.

claims.claim: Selecting a policy on the Retention policies page opens a flyout showing distribution status.
claims.quote: You can always check the distribution status of the retention policy by selecting it from the Retention policies page in the Microsoft Purview portal. From the flyout pane, if you see (Error) included in the status

claims.claim: The two printed policy cmdlets belong to Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: MC1481313 recommends updating internal compliance documentation and administrator guidance.
claims.quote: Update internal compliance documentation and administrator guidance as needed.

claims.claim: MC1481313 recommends informing compliance and records management stakeholders.
claims.quote: Inform compliance and records management stakeholders of this change.

claims.claim: The billing setup control named in the governance checklist is represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Set up pay-as-you-go billing if it is not in place'. The two controls rows cover policy inventory and Copilot retention configuration, not billing setup.

This keeps the verified prerequisite without instructing readers to configure a control absent from the table.
